title: One Usage page for every subscription's limits

body:
## Why
On 2026-10-13, after LOOM_REPOS grew from 7 to 18 repos, each station pass made 150 to 350 GitHub requests, once a minute, against an hourly budget of 5,000 shared with the brains. The budget ran out within the hour and every read failed with 403 until the reset (`publish_lanes failed ... 403`, `post_metrics failed ... 403`, `hand_back failed ... 403`): no claims, no reports, no factory landings for the rest of the hour. The pass interval was raised to 180 s by hand as a stopgap. Adding repos is supposed to be one config line (north star 9), so the station must stay inside its budget at any repo count. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- Measure first: log each pass's requests by endpoint kind (issues list, pulls list, comments, check runs, graphql) so the PR names what dominates.
- Conditional requests: list reads that repeat every pass (open issues and pulls per repo, labels) send `If-None-Match` with the last ETag; a 304 does not count against the budget. The client already stores ETags for some reads; use them everywhere a list is re-read.
- A budget guard: read `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` from responses; below a floor (for example 15% of the limit), a pass does only claims and reports and skips scans that can wait (backlog triage, metrics, standups), saying so once.
- Repos with nothing in flight (no briefed, running or pr tickets) are scanned at most every 10 minutes, not every pass.
- `lanes/mac/install.sh`: the station's interval comes from `LOOM_STATION_INTERVAL` (default 60).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: a repeated list read sends If-None-Match and treats 304 as unchanged; below the floor a pass skips the deferrable work and still claims; an idle repo is scanned once per 10 minutes; each fails without the change.
- [ ] The PR states the per-pass request count before and after on the 18-repo set, from the new log line.
- [ ] Live proof: a full hour at a 60 s interval with 18 repos and no 403 in the station log.

Size: M

## Measured
Per-pass GitHub requests on the 18-repo set, from the station's `requests:` log line:
- Before (last 40 passes before the deploy, every request counted): median 327, range 156 to 1032.
- After (first 47 passes after the deploy): median 22 counted, range 7 to 196; the rest answered 304 and did not count.
- A full hour at a 60 s interval (2026-10-14 00:00Z to 00:59Z): no 403 in the station log; 4,323 of 5,000 left at the end.

## Out of scope
A GitHub App token (a separate budget); the brains' own request use.

body:
## Why
Whakk has asked the guild for help with Klaven's Tower 7 times in 19 hours and drawn no yes. The live rows show why. Over four days the Cave guild posted 51 class quest asks: all 51 were cancelled, none drew a yes, and none was ever called to the server. The <redacted> guild posted 265 asks in the same window and drew yes answers on 93 of them.

Root cause: the guild jobs pass runs once per cohort, this process's own first and then each other family's (`_for_other_families`). Each run set `self._class_helps` and `self._classquest_held` outright, so the last cohort's plan replaced the others'. The Cave pass listed Whakk's help (20:23:29Z), the social pass posted the ask (20:23:33Z), and the <redacted> pass replaced the helps (20:23:43Z). On the next social pass (20:24:34Z) `classask._ended` found no help for the asker and cancelled the ask. No guildmate got a pass to answer it, and the escalation to random bots (from try 3) never ran, because that also needs the ask to live past its first pass.

## Summary
- `bridge._keep_class_plan` keeps each cohort's helps and class quest holds under its cohort key, the way `_class_owed_by` already does, and sets `_class_helps` and `_classquest_held` to the union of every cohort's last pass.
- `_plan_guild_jobs` calls it in place of the two outright assignments.
- Tests: a live ask posted for one cohort's member is no longer cancelled after a second cohort's job pass, and a cohort's next pass replaces only its own helps.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `test_an_ask_survives_the_next_cohorts_job_pass` fails on the old replace-outright semantics (`50 unexpectedly found in (50,)`, the ask cancelled) and passes with the fix
- [ ] The full CI check passes (ruff check, ruff format --check, compile_check, 11,789 unit tests)
- [ ] After deploy, Cave class quest asks in `orchestrator_guild_ask` live past their first social pass: some end `expired`, get a yes, or get a public channel call, where today 51 of 51 are `cancelled`

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The `/dev/api/v2/stuck` read that still reports a member stuck while its quest yields to leveling
- A cohort that leaves the roster keeps its last helps until restart, as `_class_owed_by` already does
- Respecs or granted help (natural progression only)

Refs ISSUE-871

body:
## Why
Loom has no merge queue and no global lock, and should not grow one: lanes merge as soon as their own PR is green and reviewed. The cost is that two changes that are each green can break the default branch together, and today nothing notices: the default branch's own checks after a factory merge are never read, and a red one stays red until a person or a brain happens to look. North star 5 asks that no regression stays shipped more than 2 hours unfixed or unreverted. The safety net for merging without a lock is testing after the merge and before the deploy, with an automatic bisect and revert. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- Each station pass, for each repo the factory merged into in the last 6 hours, read the combined check state of the default branch's head and of each factory merge commit since the last green one (API only, no checkout).
- When the head is red: find the first red merge commit after the last green one (a bisect over commits that already have check runs; a commit with no runs yet is waited on). If it is a factory merge whose PR head was green, and no newer commit turned the branch green within 30 minutes, brief a revert ticket for it on the fastest free lane of its repo's tier, rung 0: "Revert <sha>: <title>" whose What is `git revert --no-edit <sha>` and whose Acceptance criteria are the failing check passing. The revert ticket is `class: logic`, labeled `loom:revert`, and the factory merges it on green without waiting on medium or low findings.
- The original ticket gets a comment naming the red check and the revert ticket, and goes back to `loom:briefed` on its lane to redo the change on the new default branch.
- At most one open revert per repo; one log line per decision.
- The station's auto-deploy of Loom itself already waits for green CI; it also skips a commit that a revert ticket names.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests with recorded check states: green to red across three merges reverts the first red one; a red that a later commit fixes within 30 minutes reverts nothing; a red commit not merged by the factory reverts nothing and is reported once; a second red while a revert is open waits. Each fails without the change.
- [ ] The bisect makes no git checkout and reads at most one check-run page per commit per pass.
- [ ] Live: a deliberate breaking change on a scratch branch protected like the default branch is reverted by the factory within 45 minutes of turning red (station log, the revert PR and the green check).

Size: L

## Out of scope
A merge queue or global lock; reverting runtime regressions measured by a goal (the brain's regression slot covers those).

+"""The revert pass: a default branch a factory merge turned red is reverted.
+
+Loom has no merge queue and no global lock: a lane pull request lands as
+soon as it is green and reviewed on its own. Two changes that are each green
+can still break the default branch together, and without this pass a red
+branch stays red until a person or a brain looks (north star 5: no
+regression stays shipped more than 2 hours unfixed or unreverted). Each
+station pass, for each repo with a lane pull request merged in the last
+RECENT seconds, it reads the check runs of the default branch's newest
+commits, from the head back to the last green one (the API only, no
+checkout, one check-run page per commit per pass):
+
+- A head that is green, or whose newest result is still running, needs
+  nothing. A commit with no check runs yet, younger than NO_RUNS_WAIT, is
+  waited on; an older one (CI never ran, or every run was cancelled) is
+  skipped as untested.

+    conclusion = {"green": "success", "red": "failure", "cancelled": "cancelled"}[state]

+            "completed_at": iso(ago)}

## Intent
Class: sensitive
- A pull request whose only ticket reference names another repo now has no ticket in the factory pass, with no "no ticket for" log line each pass.
- Conflicting ticket references in one pull request still log their "no ticket for" line.

## Why
`station.log` repeats `factory: no ticket for <repo>#<n>: ticket and pull request must be in the same repository` on every pass for pull requests whose body ends with `Refs <other repo>#<n>`. body:
## Why
A ladder ticket whose rung has no lane to run on waits out the limit, however long it lasts. `_step_aside` moves a rung ticket only to another lane of the same rung. agy is the only lane of the Gemini 4 Argon high rung, and on 2026-10-19 an account quota limited that model until 2026-10-20 12:14Z. Two fix rounds pinned to that rung (ISSUE-665 for PR ISSUE-827, link-bonder ISSUE-270 for PR ISSUE-300) logged "waits on lane agy, at a limit: no free lane in its rung" every pass. Their pull requests have been open since 2026-10-18, past the 6-hour Flow target.

## Summary
- `bus/factory.py`: `RUNG_LIMIT_WAIT` (2 hours) and `_rung_waits_long`. Each lane of the rung for this repo must be down, or hold the rung's model limited past `now + RUNG_LIMIT_WAIT`. A lane at a limit with no known end does not count.
- When no lane of its rung is free and the rung waits long, `_step_aside` calls `_climb` with `failed_here=False` and `skip=rung`, under the head "Not a failure". The ticket moves to its next untried rung with a lane up, the rung it left stays untried, and no attempt is spent. When nothing is climbable it waits as before.
- A limit under two hours still waits, as `test_a_rung_ticket_whose_model_is_limited_on_its_only_lane_waits` pins.
- New test: a Gemini 4 Argon high ticket on agy, limited for a day, moves to another strong rung with the "Not a failure" note and no failed move. It fails on main and passes here; the full suite passes (2344).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A ladder ticket whose rung serves no lane within two hours climbs to an untried rung that has a lane up, with no attempt spent.
- [x] A rung whose limit lifts within two hours, or whose lane limit has no known end, keeps the ticket waiting.
- [x] The new test fails without the change and passes with it.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Queued tickets pinned to a model no lane serves (ISSUE-528 waits for gpt-6-sol).
- The two-hour threshold as a setting.

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- loom:factory label added to LABELS in labels.py, so ensure_labels creates it in repos where it does not exist
- _closed_incidents now lists closed factory incidents by the body marker instead of the loom:factory label, so incidents filed without the label are still found and their held tickets re-queued
- backlog triage now skips open issues whose body carries the factory incident marker, leaving them unlabeled
Files: 1 sensitive, 2 logic, 3 tests

## Why
Tickets held for a factory incident are never released, because the incident's label does not exist. `lanes/run_lane.sh` `file_factory_incident` creates the incident with `--label loom:factory` and, when that fails, retries without a label. The station's release path, `_closed_incidents` in `bus/station.py`, lists only closed issues with `labels=loom:factory`. The label `loom:factory` is not in `LABELS` in `bus/labels.py`, so `ensure_labels` never creates it, and on 2026-10-19 at 02:46Z `GET /repos/example/loom/labels/loom:factory` answered 404. Every incident (ISSUE-683, ISSUE-741, ISSUE-751, ISSUE-860) was filed with no label, so closing one could never re-queue its tickets.
At 02:46Z the station's held-ticket state listed 13 tickets held this way: ISSUE-575, ISSUE-850, ISSUE-528, ISSUE-585 (ISSUE-860, the unittest base check, red since 10-18 20:4xZ and fixed on main by ISSUE-859, still holding them), 7 infra tickets on ISSUE-741, 2 game-orchestrator tickets on ISSUE-683 since 10-17 21:55Z, and 1 media-library ticket on ISSUE-751. All of them read as `loom:running` for 7 to 57 hours in `bus.brain status` while no lane worked them. The triage pass also labelled three of the unlabelled incidents `loom:triage` and posted "this issue is not a ticket yet" on them.
The brain created the label and labelled the four incidents by hand at 02:46Z.

## Summary
- Add `loom:factory` to `LABELS` in `bus/labels.py`, so `ensure_labels` creates it in every repo it runs on.
- Make `_closed_incidents` in `bus/station.py` find closed incidents by the `<!-- loom:factory-incident v1 -->` body marker, without requiring the label (for example list closed issues by the incident title prefix or by the factory login, then filter on the marker).
- Make backlog triage skip an issue whose body carries the incident marker.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: `ensure_labels` on a repo with no `loom:factory` label creates it; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test in `tests/test_bus_station.py`: a closed incident issue with the marker and no labels is returned by `_closed_incidents`, and a ticket held for it is re-queued by `_release_held`; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test: triage leaves an open issue with the incident marker and no `loom:` label alone (no `loom:triage`, no comment).
- [ ] Live: after the deploy, the next closed factory incident re-queues its held tickets within one station pass (station log line "factory release: ... re-queued after incident ... closed").
Size: S

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Fixing the causes of the incidents themselves (the infra `uvx` environment fault on ISSUE-741 is its own work).
- Changing how the lane runner files or updates an incident.
Part of ISSUE-851

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- When no lane of a medium ticket's tier is up, a limit move or a queued assignment falls back to claude when it is free, else to a free easy lane (spark first), from the new FALLBACK table next to TIERS.
- A fallback move says so in its ticket note and station log line ("fallback: no medium lane is up").
- A <redacted> repo's ticket never falls back to a PUBLIC_ONLY lane; with none free it waits where it is.
- A ticket moved by fallback keeps its Difficulty: line, so its next move returns it to its own tier once a lane of it is up.
- A tier with a lane up but busy is still waited for, not fallen back from; easy and hard tiers have no fallback.
- docs/<redacted>.md (Lane choice) describes the fallback order, and a test keeps it in step with FALLBACK.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
On 2026-10-14 from about 06:00Z every lane of the medium tier (`TIERS["medium"]` in bus/factory.py: codex, codex-2, the four opencode-go slots and the anthropic slots) was at a limit at once: the ChatGPT usage limit, the OpenCode Go weekly limit and the empty API credit. Medium tickets then had no lane to move to and waited hours, while the free lanes (openrouter, workersai, zai, zen) and the spark lane sat idle (north star 3 Spread: at least 80% of slots busy whenever work is queued; north star 1 Flow). Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- When no lane of a ticket's tier is available, the factory's tier move (limit moves, stalls and queued assignment) falls back in this order: the next harder tier's available lanes (medium falls back to hard: claude), then the easier tier's available lanes (medium falls back to easy: spark and the free lanes), keeping the PUBLIC_ONLY rule for <redacted> repos. A fallback move says so in its note ("fallback: no medium lane is up").
- A ticket moved by fallback goes back to its own tier on its next move when a lane of its tier is available again.
- docs/<redacted>.md (Lane choice) describes the order.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: with every medium lane at a limit, a medium ticket moves to claude when it is free, else to a free easy lane; a <redacted> repo's ticket never falls back to a PUBLIC_ONLY lane; with a medium lane up again, the next move returns it to the tier. Each fails without the change.
- [ ] The fallback order is defined once next to TIERS and read by every tier move.
- [ ] Live: the next time a whole tier is at a limit, the station log shows fallback moves and the free lanes take work.

Size: M

## Out of scope
The model ladder for failed tickets; adding lanes.

---
Loom ticket example.factory-271, lane claude, model claude-opus-5-5.
Refs ISSUE-271

## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Before merging a lane pull request, the factory checks whether its base is behind main (the compare API's `behind_by`, or the pull request's `mergeable_state` of `behind`).
- When it is behind, the factory updates the branch (`PUT /repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}/update-branch`) and waits for checks and the review bot on the new head, instead of merging the stale head.
- One log line per update. A pull request that cannot be updated cleanly goes back for a fix round, as a conflict does today.
Files: 2 sensitive, 1 logic, 3 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The factory merges a lane pull request whose branch is behind main, so two pull requests that each passed alone can break main together. On 2026-10-19:
- issue 284 of another repo merged at 23:19Z.
- issue 285 of another repo merged at 23:44Z. Its lane had validated it against the older base, and the repo's check workflows did not run on it again after ISSUE-284 landed.
Main went red with `F821 Undefined name MediaType`, and the app's deploy-web job failed. Every lane run on the repo then stopped at its base check behind factory incident issue 1040 of this repo. The station's revert step logged "main is red ... only from checks that never ran on ISSUE-285 ... nothing reverted", so nothing fixed it until an operator session did (issue 288 of another repo).

## Summary
- Before merging a lane pull request, the factory checks whether its base is behind main (the compare API's `behind_by`, or the pull request's `mergeable_state` of `behind`).
- When it is behind, the factory updates the branch (`PUT /repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}/update-branch`) and waits for checks and the review bot on the new head, instead of merging the stale head.
- One log line per update. A pull request that cannot be updated cleanly goes back for a fix round, as a conflict does today.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: a ready pull request whose base is behind main is updated, not merged, in that pass, and merges in a later pass once its new head is green and reviewed. It fails on main.
- [ ] A test: a ready pull request that is up to date with main merges as before, with no update call.
- [ ] Live: for a week after the deploy, no lane merge turns a repo's main red from a check that passed on the pull request's own head (station revert and watch logs).
Size: M

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Requiring up-to-date branches in branch protection (repo config through Pulumi).
- The repo-side check workflow path filters.
Part of ISSUE-705

## Intent
Class: logic
- Spark usage records read each slot's hold end as an absolute epoch and report expired holds as inactive.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The usage collector (ISSUE-289) reports the spark lane's heat hold from `state/usage/spark.limit`, whose first field is an absolute epoch (when the hold ends). `_spark_records` in bus/usage.py passes it to `_utc_epoch` as a relative number of seconds, so on 2026-10-14 an expired hold showed as a thermal hold resetting in the year 2083 instead of "no active hold". The Usage page (ISSUE-296) would show that to the operator.

## Summary
- `_spark_records` reads the limit file's end time as an absolute epoch. A hold whose end time has passed is reported as no active hold (used_pct null, note "no hold"); an active one reports its real end time and reason.
- Every spark slot (spark, spark-2) gets its own record from its own `<slot>.limit` file.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a limit file ending 10 minutes from now reports a hold resetting at that time.
- [ ] A test with a limit file that ended an hour ago reports no active hold.
- [ ] A test shows spark and spark-2 each read their own limit file.

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- Other providers' records.
- The thermal guard.

## Why
docs/<redacted>.md says an easy ticket never runs on anthropic or claude, and a <redacted> repo's easy ticket runs only on spark or opencode-go. The factory's limit move (`Factory._step_aside`) ignores both: it sends a ticket off a lane at a limit to the next model ladder rung, whose first rung is the claude lane. On 2026-10-13 the spark endpoint went down during its first ticket, a one-line easy change in a <redacted> repo, and the factory moved it to claude, where it ran on the operator's own subscription. A limit is not a failure, so it should not climb the ladder at all. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- A ticket moved off a lane at a limit goes to a free lane in its own difficulty tier, using the same tier lists as docs/<redacted>.md (one table in code that the doc test reads): easy goes to spark, then opencode-go, openrouter or workersai, with zen, zai and agy on public repos only; medium goes to codex or opencode-go, and an anthropic slot only when those are full; hard goes to anthropic, claude or codex.
- It never adds a rung marker: the ladder stays for failures.
- With no free lane in the tier, the ticket waits where it is, for the lane to come back.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with an easy ticket in a <redacted> repo on a spark lane at a limit moves it to opencode-go and never to claude or anthropic; the same ticket in a public repo may go to zen; it fails without the change.
- [ ] A test shows no rung marker is posted by a limit move, and an easy ticket with no free lane in its tier stays on its lane.
- [ ] Live proof: the next limit move in the station log names a lane in the ticket's tier.

Size: S

## Out of scope
The ladder for failed or stuck tickets; the spark endpoint's own crash (tracked in the infra repo); lane heartbeats.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Deploy checks now explain when CI is pending, failed, or unreadable.
- Deploy REST reads now use the configured Loom App installation token, with gh fallback.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
`lanes/mac/station.sh` deploys a merged change before each pass only when `gh api .../check-runs?check_name=unittest` says success. When that call fails, for example at 0 REST budget, the verdict is empty, and `[ "$verdict" = success ] || return 0` skips the deploy without a word. That looks the same as "CI still running". The runtime then stays on an old revision while settings that need the new code sit loaded and inert. Both of the deploy's `gh api` calls (check runs, then revert tickets), every pass, use the operator's token rather than the Loom App's. That operator budget hit 0 several times on 2026-10-17.

## Summary
- Log why a deploy did not happen whenever the target is newer than the checkout: "waiting: unittest is in_progress on <sha>", "not deploying: the CI check could not be read (<reason>)", and so on.
- Make the deploy's GitHub calls use the Loom App installation token when the App settings are present, as `bus/github.py` does, falling back to `gh` otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a fake `gh` that fails shows station.sh printing a "could not be read" line and not deploying; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test shows a pending CI check printing a "waiting" line with the check's state.
- [ ] Live: with the App configured, a deploy pass makes no request on the operator's REST budget (its remaining count is unchanged across a pass that deploys).
Size: S

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing which check gates a deploy.
- The pin pass.
Part of ISSUE-703

## Intent
Class: sensitive
- An out-of-credit limit on any anthropic slot now marks all eight anthropic slots unavailable with the same until time, so the factory's limit move and the brief guard skip them.
- The shared credit set (SHARED_CREDIT) is defined once in bus/factory.py and read by lanes/run_lane.sh.
- A lane's out-of-credit and provider-limit heartbeats now start with "limit:" so the station sees them as limits.
- limit_held tests for the limit file before reading it, so a missing file no longer prints "No such file or directory".
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The eight anthropic slots share one API credit. When it ran out on 2026-10-13, ISSUE-209 made "out of credit" a 24-hour hold, but only on the slot that hit it: on 2026-10-14 at 01:19Z the station still moved a ticket off a codex limit onto anthropic-4, which had never run since the credit ran out, so the run failed at once and cost a retry; the same happened with another ticket the same minute. Each untried slot repeats this. Also, `limit_held` in `lanes/run_lane.sh` reads a limit file that does not exist yet, and bash prints "No such file or directory" into each slot's service log every pass (the `2>/dev/null` comes after the input redirection, so it does not cover it). Size: S

## Out of scope
Buying or topping up credit; codex limits.

title: An empty API credit holds every slot that shares it, not only the slot that hit it

body:
## Why

A second operator is about to run their own Loom against repos this Loom also scans. Loom had no notion of an issue or goal that belongs to another operator: triage, the factory, the station's claim and pull request adoption act on any issue their filters match, so two factories would label, brief and build the same issue. Adding an operator should be configuration, not a fork.

## Summary

- `bus/tickets.py`: `owned_elsewhere(issue, authors)` names the owner when an issue's assignees and `claim:<login>` labels name only logins outside `LOOM_BRIEF_AUTHORS`; `goal_operator` / `goal_ours` read an `Operator: <login>` line from a goal home's header (above its first heading); `operator_login` is the first `LOOM_BRIEF_AUTHORS` login that is not an app.
- `bus/station.py`: the claim skips a ticket owned elsewhere (checked on the listed issue and again on the fresh re-read) and a ticket whose goal names another operator; the verify picker and adoption skip owned issues and pull requests; `_goal_issues` drops goal homes that name another operator, so triage, rewrites, adoption, reports, standups and invariants leave them out. Each skip is logged once (`state/station/owned.json`). A claim assigns the ticket to the operator login and adds `claim:<login>` with its relabel, creating the label once a pass (a 422 means it exists).
- `bus/factory.py`: `_trusted` also requires the item not be owned elsewhere, so queue routing and the pull request pass leave another operator's tickets alone.
- `bus/brain.py`: triage skips an owned issue; `move` refuses to queue, brief or run one, so the brain's own CLI cannot take it either. `bus/rewrite.py`: `candidates` skips owned issues.
- `docs/LANES.md` gains "Two Looms on shared repos"; `docs/BRAIN.md` Trust names the new skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TwoLoomsTest.test_a_ticket_assigned_to_another_operator_is_not_claimed`, `test_a_queued_ticket_assigned_elsewhere_gets_no_lane`, `test_triage_skips_an_issue_assigned_elsewhere`, `test_adoption_skips_a_pull_request_assigned_elsewhere` and `test_the_verify_picker_skips_a_shipped_ticket_assigned_elsewhere` pass and fail on main.
- [ ] `test_a_claim_label_for_another_login_is_skipped_like_an_assignment` and `test_triage_adoption_and_rewrite_skip_a_claim_label_for_another_login` pass and fail on main; `test_a_claim_label_for_our_own_login_is_claimed` passes; `test_a_claim_adds_and_creates_the_operator_claim_label` fails on main.
- [ ] `test_a_goal_home_naming_another_operator_is_not_worked` and `test_a_ticket_under_another_operators_goal_is_not_claimed` fail on main; `test_a_goal_home_naming_our_operator_is_worked` passes.
- [ ] Live, after the station deploys this: an issue assigned to another collaborator in a shared repo gets no Loom label or claim from this Loom for 24 hours, read from GitHub.

Proof: on main, 11 of the 14 `TwoLoomsTest` tests fail (the 3 that pass are the "ours is still worked" baselines), and the 4 helper tests error or fail. Full suite on this branch: 1661 tests, OK (1 skipped).

Size: M

## Out of scope

- Splitting lane capacity between operators on one machine.
- Goal-level ownership in the factory's queue routing (a ticket under another operator's goal is still never claimed by the station; the factory routes on assignment and claim labels).

Refs ISSUE-649

+    to that login (docs/LANES.md, "Two Looms on shared repos"). A Loom acts

title: Two Looms share repos safely: an issue or goal another operator owns is left alone

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- A ticket may carry an "After:" header naming the tickets it builds on ("ISSUE-5", "other-repo ISSUE-7, ISSUE-8"), written by bus.brain brief --after and refused with a message when it is not a list of tickets.
- The station never claims a ticket while any ticket named in its After: line is not merged (its state label is before merged, or it cannot be read); it reads each named ticket once a pass, from its own repo.
- A named ticket closed as not planned releases the hold, and the station says so on the waiting ticket in one comment, once per named ticket.
- A ticket held by After: is not counted as stalled by the factory, so it climbs no rung of the model ladder; a hold older than 48 hours is reported to the brain once, with a comment naming the tickets it waits for and the needs-brain label.
- bus.brain status lists what every held ticket waits for, and marks a hold older than 48 hours as stuck; bus.brain escalate refuses a held ticket.
- The After: line is settled before a claim and left out of the brief the lane reads, like Not before:.
Files: 2 sensitive, 2 logic, 4 tests, 3 docs

## Why
Tickets often build on each other (a screen needs the package and the data it renders). Briefs can only say `Not before: <time>`, which is a guess: too early and the lane works on a base without the code it needs; too late and lanes sit idle. A ticket should be able to wait for the tickets it builds on.

## Summary
- A new brief header `After: #N[, #M ...]` (same repo, or `owner/name#N`), validated in bus/tickets.py like the others, and accepted by `bus.brain brief --after`.
- The station never claims a ticket while any ticket named in `After:` is not yet merged (its state label is before `merged`, or it is open without a merged pull request). A named ticket that is closed not planned releases the hold and says so in a comment.
- `bus.brain status` lists held tickets with what they wait for. A hold older than 48 hours is reported to the brain like a stuck ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test shows that a queued ticket with `After: ISSUE-5` is not claimed while ISSUE-5 is in `pr`, and is claimed once ISSUE-5 is `merged`.
- [ ] A test shows that `After:` naming a ticket closed not planned releases the hold with a comment.
- [ ] A test shows that a malformed `After:` value is refused by `bus.brain brief` with a message.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Dependencies across goals' caps or priorities.
- Changing `Not before:`.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The station files one rolling roll-pin-off invariant issue listing every goal home whose body names a roll but that no LOOM_ROLL_SHIP_DOCS entry names, so a roll source-pin pass left unconfigured is raised instead of skipped in silence.
- The issue says when LOOM_ROLL_SHIP_DOCS is empty (the pass is off), and names the fix: a loom-roll-pins block in each ship document and an entry per goal home in the station environment.
- README.md (Roll source pins) and docs/LANES.md (Invariants) describe the new invariant.
Files: 3 logic, 1 tests, 2 docs

## Why
A module change merged for a <redacted> roll sat 9.5 hours before anyone
started the roll: issue 36 of another repo (the Deadmines chest fix) merged at
06:20Z on 2026-10-16, and the source-pin pull request for roll 59 was only
opened at 15:37Z, by hand, by a brain tick. Step 2 of the WoW roll document
(bump the source pins in the deployment repo, which starts the image
build) is mechanical: it moves three known locations to the new module SHAs
and restarts nothing. While it waits for a brain to notice, the fix sits
unbuilt and the next family window passes with nothing to pin.

## Summary
When a pull request merges on a module repo that a goal ships through a
<redacted> roll (game-module, dungeon-module), the station opens the
source-pin pull request in the deployment repo within 15 minutes, using the
goal's ship document for the paths to move, and reports the build run it
started on the goal home. The brain then only reviews, proves and pins.
When a source-pin pull request for an older merge is already open, the
station updates that one instead of opening a second.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A test: a merge event on a roll-shipped module repo produces one source-pin pull request that moves exactly the pinned SHA locations the ship document names, and a second merge before it lands updates the same pull request
- [x] A test: a merge on a repo no goal ships by roll opens nothing
- [ ] Live: the next module merge on the WoW goal has its source-pin pull request open within 15 minutes of the merge (merge time and PR creation time read from the REST API), and the goal home journal names the build run

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Merging the source-pin pull request, reading digests, the prove step and
  the image pin (they stay with the brain and its gates)

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Read each holder's free bag slots before an equip that displaces worn gear. A two-hander over a one-hand weapon and shield needs one free slot for the shield.
- When the bags are full, queue a make-room job before the equip. Sell safe junk first, then use the existing material mail, sale, or destroy ladder. Queue the equip as soon as room appears.
- Record a shortage even if the first room read failed, so an existing refusal hold lifts when a slot is freed. Explain a shortage that cannot be cleared in the member's plan.

## Why
A full bag blocks an equip that must move an additional worn piece into inventory. The prior retry policy held the resulting refusal for 24 hours.

## Summary
Make room for the equip, then retry when the slot is free.

## Cause and measured impact
At the 2026-10-18 17:00Z read, three members had been held 8.6 to 10.8 hours on refused two-hander equips. Each had six refusals in the preceding 48 hours. Each wore a one-hand weapon and shield, and each had zero free bag slots: two had 16 of 16 backpack slots filled, and one had 22 of 22 total slots filled. InventoryResult 21 was the game's refusal to swap two worn pieces into the one slot vacated by the wanted item. After the third refusal, the retry schedule waited 24 hours, while the shortage remained.

The make-room job frees a slot by selling or moving an allowed carried stack. The next equip pass then queues the two-hander, so the affected count falls when the game accepts the equip and the members stop waiting. This does not change the health endpoint or its threshold. Live absence for 24 hours remains to be observed after shipping.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Name the measured cause and how the affected count falls.
- [x] A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- [ ] Live finding absent from the health endpoint for 24 hours after shipping.

Size: M

## Out of scope
Other health findings have separate tickets.

## Verification
- The full-backpack, worn-shield regression test fails before the slot check and passes with it.
- A second regression test failed on this branch before the follow-up fix: if the first room read failed, an existing hold did not lift after room was made. It now passes.
- Local validation: ruff, compile check, and the full unittest suite.

## Follow-up
These members at levels 21 to 37 had no spare bag capacity. Bag purchasing has a separate pass; review why they still had no bag upgrade separately from this equip refusal fix.

Refs ISSUE-1088

body:
## Why
Refs ISSUE-870, ISSUE-868. After 4.7 hours of walk restarts, the roster showed the leader with stuck false, waiting "" and for_s 17033. nowstatus._from_intent (nowstatus.py:572) reports restarts only while the intent row holds a walk. Between restarts the row reads none, so _live (nowstatus.py:611) falls back to the step "the dungeon run ended walking...", which has no waiting reason, and hold_blocker (apiv2/members.py:267) needs one, so the unstuck loop never counts this member.

## Summary
- When _restarts(steps) is 3 or more inside the window, compose reports the walk as doing and "a way there; the walk has ended and restarted N times" as waiting, whether or not the intent row is set at that moment. The clock starts at the first restart.
- hold_blocker gives kind "walk restarts" for that reading once it has held HOLD_STUCK_SECONDS.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New test in tests/test_now_status.py, test_restarts_reported_between_restarts: intent current_kind "none" plus a fresh "took over" step with 424 occurrences gives a waiting reason containing "restarted 424 times"; it fails on main
- [ ] A members test: hold_blocker returns kind "walk restarts" for that reading after 30 minutes and None before; existing now-status tests pass
- [ ] Live proof: /api/v2/stuck lists a member whose walk keeps restarting, with kind "walk restarts" and a since equal to the first restart

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The module-side causes (game-module tickets)
- The roster page layout

body:
## Intent
Class: tests
- tests/test_sdlc_doc.py reads docs/SDLC.md and fails when the eight stage headings move, a backticked module path or loom:/class: label is not in the tree or bus/labels.py, a live principle names no module, or a planned principle cites no single ticket as #N or cites one this branch's history already
- docs/SDLC.md moves the six principles whose tickets merged (change class and Intent section, merge rules by class, bisected revert of a red default branch, the goal home Trunk line, the component log watcher, the leak-scan text repair) into Live principles, each naming the module that carries it.
- docs/SDLC.md moves stage handoff journaling and lane retry limits into Live principles with bus/handoff.py, bus/journal.py and bus/station.py, and drops the lane-specific brief constraints bullet, which had no code and no ticket behind it.
- docs/SDLC.md lists as planned the four open, unmerged tickets ISSUE-259, ISSUE-261, ISSUE-262 and ISSUE-263 instead of ISSUE-227, ISSUE-228 and ISSUE-229, whose work had already merged.
- docs/SDLC.md cites the proof comment as the <!-- loom:proof v1 --> marker bus/proof.py writes instead of a loom:proof label the bus never defines, and drops the BRIEFED constant bus/labels.py never had.
Files: 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
ISSUE-226 asked for docs/SDLC.md plus a test that keeps it honest. PR 234 merged the doc and its links but no test, so the doc can drift from the code unnoticed, and ISSUE-226 cannot be verified. Since then most of its "Planned principles" have merged (change classes and the Intent section, merge rules by class, post-merge bisect and revert, the goal home Trunk line, the component log watcher, the leak-scan text repair), so the live and planned marks are already wrong. Refs ISSUE-226. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- `tests/test_sdlc_doc.py` (a `unittest.TestCase`): reads docs/SDLC.md and asserts (a) the eight stage headings brief, run, PR, review, merge, after merge, deploy, verify exist under `## Stages`; (b) every backticked `bus/...` or `lanes/...` path in the doc exists in the repo; (c) every backticked `loom:...` or `class:...` label in the doc is defined in `bus/labels.py`; (d) every principle listed under "Planned principles" cites an open ticket as `#N`.
- docs/SDLC.md: move each principle whose ticket merged into "Live principles" with the module that does it; leave a principle planned only with its open ticket number.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `tests/test_sdlc_doc.py` fails on the current main (stale marks or a missing path or label) and passes after the doc update.
- [ ] Every principle under "Live principles" names the module that implements it, and every planned one cites an open ticket.
- [ ] The full suite passes in CI.

Size: S

## Out of scope
Rewriting the stage descriptions beyond what the test requires.

 Once verified, the ticket is closed and marked `loom:verified`. If verification fails, the ticket re-enters the lifecycle.
 
 ## Principles
 
+A live principle names the module that carries it. A planned one is not in the tree
+yet and cites the open ticket that tracks it.
+
 ### Live principles
 
-- **No merge queue or global lock**: Each change proceeds independently; the factory's lane order determines priority, not a merge queue.
-- **Default branch tested after each merge**: CI verifies the merged state immediately; failures trigger auto-revert.
-- **Deploy health vigilance**: Failed deploys and 5xx/SSL endpoints halt progress until resolved.
-- **Proof-based closure**: Tickets require a `loom:proof` comment documenting how acceptance criteria were met.
+- **No merge queue or global lock**: each change proceeds independently; `bus/factory.py` merges a lane pull request on its own once it is green and its review-bot threads are answered, so lane order rather than a queue sets priority.
+- **One change class per lane pull request**, written into the Intent section the runner opens: `bus/change_class.py` classifies the changed files as sensitive, logic, tests or docs (ISSUE-227).
+- **Merge rules follow the change class**: `bus/factory.py` lands a docs or tests pull request on checks and a review pass alone, and marks a sensitive one `needs-brain` for the brain instead (ISSUE-228).
+- **The default branch is judged after every merge**: CI runs on it, and a red it did not see coming is bisected back to the merge that caused it; `bus/revert.py` files that revert as a ticket, which lands before other work (ISSUE-229).
+- **A goal home's `Trunk:` line names the branch its briefs and pull requests target**: `bus/brain.py` reads the line, targets it, and warns when work is headed somewhere else (ISSUE-230).
+- **One watcher per component log**: `bus/watch.py` reduces the lines a log gained into signatures and files one ticket per new repeated error (ISSUE-231).
+- **A leak-scan failure in a lane pull request's text is repaired in the text**: `bus/factory.py` rewrites each flagged line of the title and body instead of sending the change back as code (ISSUE-232).
+- **Stage handoff journaling**: `bus/journal.py` writes the goal journal and `bus/handoff.py` reads its defer and done markers, so a peer finishes stage work a stopped brain left behind (ISSUE-103).
+- **A failed lane run retries on another lane, and a lane at its provider limit stops taking work**: `bus/station.py` counts the retry lines on the ticket, caps them at `LOOM_RETRY_MAX`, and moves the ticket to the next lane in the brain's order (ISSUE-112).
+- **Deploy health vigilance**: a failed deploy or a 5xx endpoint stops the line; `dispatch/ship.py` is the one shipper and honors the deploy caps and roll windows on the goal home, and `dispatch/verify.py` closes a shipped ticket only on live proof.
+- **Proof-based closure**: a ticket closes on a proof record checked against its own acceptance criteria; `bus/proof.py` checks the record and `bus/brain.py` posts the `<!-- loom:proof v1 -->` comment before closing.
 
 ### Planned principles
 
-- **Stage handoff journaling**: See [issue ISSUE-227](https://github.com/example/factory/issues/ISSUE-227) - full defer/done markers for each stage transition.
-- **Automated retry limits**: See [issue ISSUE-228](https://github.com/example/factory/issues/ISSUE-228) - transient and limit errors trigger automatic lane retries.
-- **Lane-specific brief constraints**: See [issue ISSUE-229](https://github.com/example/factory/issues/ISSUE-229) - lanes may specify execution constraints in brief analysis.
+- **A ticket nobody claimed moves within its tier and never climbs the ladder** (ISSUE-259).
+- **Escalation counts only work failures, and a failed pull request create is transient** (ISSUE-261).
+- **The station ships a Loom ticket when it deploys the commit that carries it** (ISSUE-262).
+- **The status and the resume list the shipped tickets due for verification, and the brain spends a share of each hour on them** (ISSUE-263).
diff --git a/tests/test_sdlc_doc.py b/tests/test_sdlc_doc.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..bd8c6817
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_sdlc_doc.py
@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+"""docs/SDLC.md must agree with the tree: its stage headings, every path and
+label it cites, and the live and planned marks on its principles.
+
+ISSUE-226 merged the document with no test behind it, so its planned principles
+kept citing tickets whose work had already merged and nobody noticed. A test
+is the only thing in this repo that reads the document on every change.
+
+CI holds no GitHub token, so "open" is not asked of the API: a planned
+principle must write its ticket out as `#N` (not hide it in a link), and must
+not cite a number this branch's history already carries. On a shallow CI
+checkout the history holds one commit, and the second half simply has less to
+look at; the shape of the citation is checked either way.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+DOC = ROOT / "docs" / "SDLC.md"
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
+
+from bus import labels  # noqa: E402
+
+STAGES = ["brief", "run", "PR", "review", "merge", "after merge",
+          "deploy", "verify"]
+
+HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6}) +(.*\S)\s*$")
+BULLET = re.compile(r"^[-*] +(\S.*)$")
+SPAN = re.compile(r"`([^`\n]+)`")
+PATH = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$")
+LABEL = re.compile(r"^(?:loom|class):[a-z0-9:_-]+$")
+TICKET = re.compile(r"#([0-9]+)\b")
+LINK_TARGET = re.compile(r"\]\([^)]*\)")
+
+
+class SdlcDoc(unittest.TestCase):
+    """docs/SDLC.md, read the way a reader reads it: headings, bullets and
+    the backticked tokens between them."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.text = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.lines = self.text.splitlines()
+
+    def section(self, title):
+        """The lines under a heading, up to the next heading at its level or
+        above: a '## Stages' section keeps its '### ' stages."""
+        out, level, inside = [], None, False
+        for line in self.lines:
+            found = HEADING.match(line)
+            if not found:
+                if inside:
+                    out.append(line)
+                continue
+            if not inside:
+                inside = found.group(2) == title
+                level = len(found.group(1))
+                continue
+            if len(found.group(1)) <= level:
+                break
+            out.append(line)
+        self.assertTrue(inside, "docs/SDLC.md has no %r heading" % title)
+        return out
+
+    def bullets(self, title):
+        return [BULLET.match(line).group(1)
+                for line in self.section(title) if BULLET.match(line)]
+
+    def spans(self):
+        return SPAN.findall(self.text)
+
+    def merged(self):
+        """Ticket numbers this branch's history already carries."""
+        log = subprocess.run(["git", "log", "--format=%s"], cwd=ROOT,
+                             capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+        if log.returncode != 0:
+            return set()
+        return set(TICKET.findall(log.stdout))
+
+    def test_the_eight_stages_are_headed_in_order(self):
+        stages = [HEADING.match(line).group(2)
+                  for line in self.section("Stages") if HEADING.match(line)]
+        self.assertEqual(stages, STAGES)
+
+    def test_every_backticked_repo_path_exists(self):
+        named = [span for span in self.spans() if PATH.match(span)]
+        self.assertTrue(named, "docs/SDLC.md names no module")
+        for span in named:
+            self.assertTrue((ROOT / span).exists(), "%s does not exist" % span)
+
+    def test_every_backticked_label_is_defined(self):
+        named = [span for span in self.spans() if LABEL.match(span)]
+        self.assertTrue(named, "docs/SDLC.md names no label")
+        for span in named:
+            self.assertTrue(span in labels.LABELS, "no label named %s" % span)
+
+    def test_every_live_principle_names_a_module(self):
+        live = self.bullets("Live principles")
+        self.assertTrue(live, "docs/SDLC.md lists no live principles")
+        for line in live:
+            named = [span for span in SPAN.findall(line) if PATH.match(span)]
+            self.assertTrue(named, "no module named: %s" % line)
+
+    def test_every_planned_principle_cites_an_open_ticket(self):
+        merged = self.merged()
+        for line in self.bullets("Planned principles"):
+            cited = TICKET.findall(LINK_TARGET.sub("", line))
+            self.assertEqual(len(cited), 1,
+                             "one ticket written out as #N: %s" % line)
+            self.assertNotIn(cited[0], merged,
+                             "already merged, so not planned: %s" % line)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
\ No newline at end of file
label: GOOD

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Combined commit-status reads that return 403 or 404 now emit a stderr notice and continue using check runs; other errors still propagate.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests

## Why
`python3 -m bus.brain fix` cannot send a pull request back on a <redacted> repo. `_failing_checks` in bus/brain.py reads `GET /repos/OWNER/NAME/commits/SHA/status`, and the brain's App gets 403 there on <redacted> repos while `.../check-runs` answers 200. The whole command aborts before it posts the fix brief. Seen 2026-10-21 14:30Z on a <redacted> repo's lane pull request: `Error: GET /repos/.../commits/07d60748.../status -> 403`. The same ruling had already failed the same way at 06:56Z and 07:43Z, so two brains journaled a send-back the factory never received, and the stage was deferred three times. The earlier station ticket for 403s is closed, and this path still fails.

## Summary
In `_failing_checks` (bus/brain.py), treat a 403 or 404 on the combined commit status as "no statuses" and go on with the check runs, which already carry every check these repos run. Write one line to stderr naming the repo and that commit statuses were not readable, so the gap stays visible. Leave the check-run read unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `bus.brain fix` on a pull request whose combined-status read answers 403 posts its fix brief, listing the failing check runs, instead of exiting with the 403 error.
- [x] A unit test with a fake GitHub whose `/commits/SHA/status` raises a 403 `GitHubError` shows `_failing_checks` returning the failing check runs and no exception.
- [x] Any other error on the status read (for example a 500) still raises as today, covered by a test.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing the GitHub App's permissions.
- The station's own status read in bus/station.py.
Part of ISSUE-1299

body:
## Why
The lane runner clones a fresh shallow tree for every brief attempt (`lanes/run_lane.sh`, `TREE="$WORKDIR/$TICKET"`) and removes it only when the same attempt name runs again, which never happens. On 2026-10-13 the lane machine's disk reached 119 MB free; 385 leftover trees held 7.8 GB of it. With the disk full, clones, logs and state writes fail for every lane.

## Summary
- New station step `prune_trees`, run every pass: removes a folder under `worktrees/` whose name is not a brief waiting or running in any lane inbox, once it has not changed for `TREE_KEEP` (one hour). The run's log stays in `logs/`; a later attempt clones its own tree.
- Uses `lstat`, so a link in the folder is removed without being followed.
- Tests: an old finished tree is removed while a running one and a fresh one stay; a link is removed and its target kept. Both fail on main. 414 passed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A finished tree older than an hour is removed and a running or fresh tree is kept (test)
- [ ] A link under `worktrees/` never leads to removing anything outside it (test)
- [ ] Live: station log shows "removed N finished lane tree(s)" and `worktrees/` stays near the number of running briefs

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The agy lane's own work folder (`LOOM_AGY_WORKDIR`), outside `worktrees/`.
- Log rotation.

Part of ISSUE-30

body:
## Why

The dashboard runs a pinned Loom revision in a deployment repo. On 2026-10-17 it ran a revision six dashboard commits behind, so a merged fix (ISSUE-551) never reached it. The station already has a pin pass (`bus/pin.py`, run from `lanes/mac/station.sh` when `LOOM_PIN_TARGETS` is set), but it bumps on every main move, whether or not the dashboard changed, and its body does not name the checksum. A pin bump should follow a dashboard change, and only a dashboard change.

## Summary

- `bus/pin.py`: `pin_one` compares the pinned revision with the new one (one compare read, reused for the merged titles) and opens or updates the pin pull request only when a file under the target's `watch` prefix changed (default `dashboard/`; a rename out of it counts, and so does a comparison GitHub cannot list in full). A merge that changes nothing there logs why and downloads nothing.
- The body names the revision and the sha256 from two matching downloads; a mismatch still opens nothing (unchanged). A new pin pull request is labelled `pin-bump`; a refused label is logged.
- `targets` accepts and validates an optional `watch` per target; `.env.example` and `docs/BRAIN.md` describe it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PinTest.test_a_dashboard_merge_opens_one_labelled_pin_pull_request_naming_commit_and_sha` (one pin-bump body naming the commit and the sha256) and `test_a_merge_touching_nothing_under_dashboard_opens_no_pin_pull_request` (a merge touching nothing under `dashboard/` produces none) pass and fail on main.
- [ ] `PinTest.test_changed_tarball_or_red_ci_opens_nothing_and_logs_reason`: the sha256 is computed twice and a mismatch opens no pull request (existing test, still passing).
- [ ] Live: the next dashboard change merged after the deploy reaches the running pod within an hour, read from the pod's fetch-loom log. This needs `LOOM_PIN_TARGETS` set on the station machine.

Proof: on main, 4 of the 4 new pin tests fail or error. Full suite on this branch: 1646 tests, OK (1 skipped).

Size: M

## Out of scope

- Other deployments.
- Moving a dashboard ticket to shipped when the pod reports its revision: Loom tickets ship at the station's own deploy today (docs/BRAIN.md, Shipping Loom itself); a pod-reported ship step needs the pod to report its revision and is left for a follow-up ticket.

Refs ISSUE-612

body:
## Why
The factory's "code changed without a test" check (`is_test` in bus/factory.py) misses tests that live in a `t/` folder or are named `TestX.cpp`, as in the C++ module repo (`t/TestBlackfathomDeeps.cpp`). On 2026-10-13 it sent two pull requests there back for a test they already had, right after their findings were deferred, costing each a lane round. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- `is_test` also counts a file under a `t`, `spec` or `__tests__` folder, and a file whose name starts with `test` in any case (`TestX.cpp`, `test_x.py`, `testutil.go`).
- Keep the existing rules (a `test`/`tests` folder, `_test.`, `.test.`, `.spec.`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test shows `t/TestBlackfathomDeeps.cpp`, `spec/a_spec.rb` and `src/__tests__/a.js` count as tests and `src/contest.py` and `src/latest.cpp` do not; it fails without the change.
- [ ] `lacks_test(["src/a.cpp", "t/TestA.cpp"])` is False.
- [ ] Live proof: the next pull request in the C++ module repo that changes a `t/` test is not sent back for a missing test.

Size: S

## Out of scope
Repos with no test harness (`LOOM_NO_TEST_REPOS`); the deferral step.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Three consecutive class quest party timeouts now make the asker level for the existing stall hold after a server try instead of asking for the same failing party again.

On 2026-10-12 Workwork had waited 27h 42m: "Cannot finish Creature of the Void alone: asked the guild for help 56 times, and nobody has come." <redacted> (Call of Fire, 2 asks) and Pokka (Taming the Beast, 4 asks) were stuck the same way. - [ ] For Workwork's ask, the reason each eligible member did not come is written here
- [ ] An ask unanswered after a set number of tries goes to the family or a PUG (test)
- [ ] No class quest help ask waits longer than 2 hours

body:
## Why

Within an hour of the factory running, it left 15 tickets "past the last rung" (loom, game-orchestrator, game-module, grug, dungeon-module). The comments show why, and no model was at fault:

- Right after a lane pushed a fix, the factory judged the pull request before the review bot had started on the new commit. It read the last head's open threads as current and sent the work back again (ISSUE-145: fixes pushed at 04:44, sent back and given up at 04:49).
- Every review round climbed a rung, even when the lane fixed everything asked and the review found new things. Conflict-only rounds climbed too, though no model could fix a conflict before the runner merged the base.

The operator's rule is to climb when work is "repeatedly stuck", not when it is moving.

## Summary

- `bus/factory.py`:
  - `_review_state` waits while the review check has not run on a head pushed within 30 minutes, so old threads are never judged against a new head.
  - `stuck()` climbs only when a thread the last `loom:fix` comment asked for is still open, when checks it asked for still fail, or when the pull request is over 6 hours old. New review findings and a conflict alone stay on the lane.
  - `rung_of` reads the latest rung marker, so a `<!-- loom:rung 0 -->` comment starts a ticket's ladder again.
- `docs/LANES.md`: the rule.
- `tests/test_bus_factory.py`: new findings stay; surviving threads and still-failing checks climb; a conflict never climbs; a fresh push waits; a rung 0 marker restarts. Four of the five fail on the old factory.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Only stuck rounds climb, and a fresh push waits for its review (tests that fail without the change)
- [ ] A rung 0 marker restarts the ladder (tests)
- [ ] Live: after this ships and the 15 tickets get a rung 0 marker, none reaches the last rung without a surviving thread, a still-failing check or 6 hours of age

Size: S

## Out of scope

- Per-thread replies
- Changing the ladder's models

Part of ISSUE-30

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The lane machine's brain records each tick step as its own lock holder and lock repo, so its steps between lock and unlock are no longer refused as a non-holder.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The Brain view shows where the current brain tick is (10 steps: lock, status, merge, verify, failed, asks, brief, triage, journal, unlock) and what it is thinking (docs/design/floor/README.md, Brain). Today nothing records the step; a reader can only guess from the journal after the tick ends. Both brains (the lane machine's tick and the scheduled <redacted> tick) follow docs/<redacted>.md, so the record must work from either.

## Summary
- `python3 -m bus.brain step NAME [--note TEXT] --holder H`: records the current step (one of the 10 names) and an optional one-line thought for the lock holder, in the brain lock's existing GitHub record (no new issue), with a UTC time. Only the lock holder may write it. One small write per step; a failed write never fails the tick.
- `python3 -m bus.brain step --show` and a library function return `{holder, started_at, step, step_index, steps, notes: [{ts, step, text}]}` for the current or last tick; `null` fields when nothing was recorded.
- docs/<redacted>.md: each numbered tick step says to run `bus.brain step` first. lanes/mac/brain.sh records `lock` and `unlock` itself.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a fake GitHub shows that `step merge --note ...` by the holder is recorded and read back with its index, and that a non-holder is refused.
- [ ] A test shows that a GitHub failure during `step` is logged and returns success, so the tick goes on.
- [ ] A test (tests/test_sdlc_doc.py style) checks that docs/<redacted>.md names `bus.brain step` for each of the 10 steps.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The Brain view itself.
- Changing what the tick does at each step.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Added the read-only Backlog view with ranked epics, URL filters, joined Loom states, and health inspectors.
- Added the byte-preserving backlog JSON endpoint and the merged Needs you queue with ask ordering and human counts.
Files: 3 logic, 1 tests

## Why
Hunt, the backlog board, merges into the dashboard (decision 0001): one place from backlog to verified, and ONE queue of things only the operator can do. Hunt's collector keeps publishing backlog.json; the dashboard renders it and serves it unchanged. Builds on ISSUE-281 and ISSUE-287. Build order step 4.

## Summary
- `/backlog`: render backlog.json (from `LOOM_BACKLOG_SOURCE`) keeping Hunt's ranking exactly: the order in the file (Cave tier, then the deterministic score); per epic: repo#number, title, tier and why, score, completeness `closed/total`, next ticket with criteria ticked/total, open children. Each child also shows its Loom state if it is a `loom:ticket` (joined from the ticket data). The start-here card names `epics[0]` and `epics[0].next`. Keep Hunt's caveman words where Hunt's data appears (Cave, Elder, markings). Filters (repo, tier) are URL query parameters.
- Backlog health inspectors, computed from the same data: epics whose children are all closed but the epic is open, children with no parent link, nonstandard titles; each as a short list with links.
- `GET /backlog.json`: the source bytes unchanged, `application/json`, same keys and order (`generated_at`, `judged_by`, `repos`, `totals`, `epics`, `needs_operator`, `ready_for_human`, `queue_comments_read`). Read-only: nothing here writes to GitHub.
- `/needs-you`: one queue merging backlog.json `needs_operator` and `ready_for_human` with Loom's open `needs-operator` issues, deduplicated by repo#number (an item in both is listed once, under needs-operator), ordered by unblocks descending then waiting_since ascending; the ask is quoted, never written; "waiting" vs "idle" by `waiting_since_source` (labeled vs updated). A footer line with `loom:human` counts by repo. Each card shows one exact ask; links open the issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test checks `/backlog.json` returns the fixture bytes unchanged and that `/backlog` lists epics in file order with `epics[0].next` in the start-here card.
- [ ] A test checks the merged Needs you queue: dedupe by repo#number, order by unblocks then waiting_since, and "idle" shown for an updated-sourced item.
- [ ] A test checks each health inspector on a fixture (finished but open, unlinked child, nonstandard title).

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Moving Hunt's collector or judge into this repo (follow-up).
- Routing Hunt's hostname (the deploy ticket).

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The station now closes a ticket as completed in the same pass it verifies it, instead of stopping at loom:verified and waiting for a separate brain.close call.
- bus/station.py: `_apply_proof` calls `brain.close(..., reason="completed")` after moving the ticket to loom:verified; if close refuses (e.g. a criterion was un-ticked after the proof was posted), the error is logged with `_say` and the ticket stays open at loom:verified.
- tests/test_bus_station.py: FakeGitHub attributes posted comments to the bot author (`self.bot`) and PATCH handler now records `state`/`state_reason` so close-as-completed can be observed; added `test_a_valid_proof_verifies_and_closes_the_ticket` and `test_a_verified_ticket_with_an_unticked_box_is_no
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
docs/SDLC.md says a verified ticket is closed, but nothing closes it. The station's verify path moves a ticket to `loom:verified` and stops, and closing is a separate brain command that brains rarely run. On 2026-10-17, 32 open tickets under the Loom goal home were verified with every acceptance box ticked and still open. They inflated the goal's child list past GitHub's 100 sub-issue cap and were closed by hand.

## Summary
When the station moves a ticket to `loom:verified` and the proof record ticks every acceptance box, it closes the ticket as completed in the same pass, through the same checks the brain's close command uses (proof present, all boxes checked). A verified ticket with any unticked box stays open, and the station logs why.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: a verify that moves a ticket to verified with all boxes ticked also closes it as completed; it fails on main.

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Brain tick steps and one-line thoughts are recorded in the GitHub lock record and can be read with step --show.
- <redacted> and lane-machine tick instructions record each step, with step-write failures kept nonfatal.
Files: 1 sensitive, 2 logic, 3 tests, 1 docs

## Why
The Brain view shows where the current brain tick is (10 steps: lock, status, merge, verify, failed, asks, brief, triage, journal, unlock) and what it is thinking (docs/design/floor/README.md, Brain). Today nothing records the step; a reader can only guess from the journal after the tick ends. Both brains (the lane machine's tick and the scheduled <redacted> tick) follow docs/<redacted>.md, so the record must work from either.

## Summary
- `python3 -m bus.brain step NAME [--note TEXT] --holder H`: records the current step (one of the 10 names) and an optional one-line thought for the lock holder, in the brain lock's existing GitHub record (no new issue), with a UTC time. Only the lock holder may write it. One small write per step; a failed write never fails the tick.
- `python3 -m bus.brain step --show` and a library function return `{holder, started_at, step, step_index, steps, notes: [{ts, step, text}]}` for the current or last tick; `null` fields when nothing was recorded.
- docs/<redacted>.md: each numbered tick step says to run `bus.brain step` first. lanes/mac/brain.sh records `lock` and `unlock` itself.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a fake GitHub shows that `step merge --note ...` by the holder is recorded and read back with its index, and that a non-holder is refused.
- [ ] A test shows that a GitHub failure during `step` is logged and returns success, so the tick goes on.
- [ ] A test (tests/test_sdlc_doc.py style) checks that docs/<redacted>.md names `bus.brain step` for each of the 10 steps.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The Brain view itself.
- Changing what the tick does at each step.

+def _step_record(message: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Read the recorded step fields from one lock commit message."""
+    current_holder = re.search(r"holder=(\S+)", message)
+    record = {"holder": current_holder.group(1) if current_holder else None,
+              "started_at": None,
+              "step": None, "step_index": None, "steps": list(TICK_STEPS), "notes": []}
+    encoded = next((line[len(STEP_MARKER):] for line in message.splitlines()
+                    if line.startswith(STEP_MARKER)), "")

+        try:

+        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):

+    return record

+def tick_step(gh: GitHub, lock_repo: str, step: Optional[str] = None,
+              note: Optional[str] = None, holder: Optional[str] = None,
+              now: Optional[datetime] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Read the tick record, or append one step to the current lock commit."""
+    now = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)
+    ref_path = "/repos/%s/git/ref/heads/%s" % (lock_repo, lock.LOCK_BRANCH)
+    ref = gh.rest("GET", ref_path, ok=(404,))
+    if ref.status == 404:
+        return _step_record("")
+    sha = ref.data["object"]["sha"]
+    commit = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s/git/commits/%s" % (lock_repo, sha), ok=(404,))
+    if commit.status == 404:
+        return _step_record("")
+    message = str(commit.data.get("message") or "")
+    record = _step_record(message)
+    if step is None:
+        return record
+    if step not in TICK_STEPS:
+        raise ValueError("step must be one of %s" % ", ".join(TICK_STEPS))
+    lock_info = lock._read_lock(gh, lock_repo)
+    if lock_info is None or lock_info[0] != holder or lock_info[1] is None or lock_info[1] <= now:
+        raise ValueError("%s does not hold the lock in %s; only the lock holder acts"
+                         % (holder, lock_repo))
+    at = _iso(now)
+    if step == "lock" or not record["started_at"]:
+        record["started_at"] = at
+        record["notes"] = []
+    record["step"] = step
+    record["step_index"] = TICK_STEPS.index(step) + 1
+    if note:
+        if "\n" in note or "\r" in note:
+            raise ValueError("note must be one line")

+    record["holder"] = holder
+    clean = "\n".join(line for line in message.splitlines() if not line.startswith(STEP_MARKER))

+        {k: record[k] for k in ("started_at", "step", "step_index", "notes")}, separators=(",", ":"))
+    created = gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/git/commits" % lock_repo, {
+        "message": new_message, "tree": commit.data["tree"]["sha"], "parents": [sha]})
+    gh.rest("PATCH", ref_path, {"sha": created.data["sha"], "force": True})
+    return record
+

+def _cmd_step(gh: GitHub, args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
+    try:

Edit README.md only. Read the lane list in the header comment of lanes/run_lane.sh and the "workersai" and "agy" sections of docs/LANES.md. Then:

## Intent
Class: logic
- GET /v1/<redacted>/{key_id} now returns `drift`: each package the device's merged install-apps names, the versionCode asked for, the one the device last reported, and a state (current, ahead, behind, absent, unreported, unreadable), with `drifted` counting the rows that are behind, absent, unreported or u
- `drift` is null for a device that never reported, and {"known": false, "reason": ...} when device-fleet cannot read the device's policy; the route stays 200 and never returns an empty list in its place.
- Packages install-apps does not name (Play-managed apps included) are never drift; nothing reads or drives Play's update queue, and docs/policy.md records why, plus how pushing a newer APK works (publish the asset, raise `version`) and why the report covers managed packages only (a fifth permission w
Files: 2 logic, 2 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The control plane needs to know what a device has installed and be able to enforce updates. Devices currently never report their installed packages, so the only way to inspect a phone is physical. After hiding the Play store on a device, Devicefleet assumed responsibility for keeping that device's apps updated but has no way to track or deliver those updates.

## Summary
Implement a check-in endpoint that authenticated devices call to report installed packages and versions. Reuse the application-layer identity proof mechanism already used by proof.py. The control plane stores reported packages in a <redacted> record and compares against expected versions to surface drift. For apps Devicefleet owns, support pushing a newer APK via Device Owner silent install. Be explicit that Play-managed apps are out of reach and do not build anything that claims to drive Play's update queue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A device reports its installed packages and versions without a cable
- [ ] Authenticated by the device identity proof mechanism, not a shared secret
- [ ] The control plane can answer 'what is on that phone' for an enrolled device
- [ ] A version behind the expected version is visible as drift
- [ ] Pushing a newer APK to an app Devicefleet owns is possible, or the reason it is not yet is recorded
- [ ] No code attempts to enumerate or drive Play's update queue

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Console rendering of the reported state (legacy no. 36)
- Diagnostics upload (legacy no. 27), which shares the channel and design
Rewritten from issue 98.

+### What device-fleet can keep current, and what it cannot
+
+Hiding the Play Store made device-fleet responsible for keeping a device's
+applications current. It can do that for the applications it ships, and only
+those (ISSUE-162).
+
+**Pushing a newer build of an application device-fleet owns** is: publish the APK
+into the asset store, then raise `version` (and the digest and asset name) on
+its `install-apps` line. At its next check-in the device sees it is behind and
+installs the new build silently as Device Owner, over its own identity, with
+no cable and nobody holding it. device-fleet's own agent updates the same way.
+
+**Whether it worked is drift.** `GET /v1/<redacted>/{key_id}` returns `drift` beside
+`report`: every package the device's `install-apps` names (merged across
+scopes exactly as it is served), the `versionCode` asked for, the one the
+device last reported, and a `state`:
+
+    current      installed at the version asked for
+    ahead        installed newer; left alone, Android refuses a downgrade
+    behind       installed older                                  (drift)
+    absent       not installed                                    (drift)
+    unreported   named now, not in the last report; policy moved on (drift)
+    unreadable   no version device-fleet can read from the line         (drift)
+
+`drifted` counts the drift rows. `drift` is null for a device that never
+reported, and `{"known": false, "reason": ...}` when device-fleet cannot read the
+device's policy - never an empty list, which would read as nothing behind.
+A row that stays `behind` across check-ins is an install that did not take,
+and the `install-apps` step's concerns in `report` say why.

+**Play-managed applications are out of reach, and nothing here pretends
+otherwise.** The expectation is `install-apps` and nothing else, so an
+application device-fleet did not ship is never drift: device-fleet cannot update it, and a
+row saying it is behind would promise something nothing here can do. A device
+device-fleet owns is not enrolled in managed Google Play (`provisioning-a-pixel.md`),
+so there is no enterprise Play update queue to drive, and
+device-fleet neither reads nor drives one. Updating such an application means
+taking it over: ship its APK through `install-apps`, signed by the key the
+installed copy was signed with.

+can see only what its manifest's `queries` block lets it see (below); listing
+every installed package needs `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, a fifth permission, and
+the four-permission profile is the only input to Play Protect's approved-DPC
+heuristic this project controls. So "what is on that phone" is answered for
+what device-fleet manages, which is also the set it can act on.

+# WHAT COUNTS AS DRIFT (ISSUE-162). `ahead` is not: the agent leaves a newer
+# build alone because Android refuses the downgrade, and a newer version is what
+# a hand-installed build looks like. `unreadable` is: device-fleet cannot read a
+# version from the line, the agent refuses it, and nothing will update it.
+_DRIFTED = frozenset({"behind", "absent", "unreported", "unreadable"})

+
+def _package_state(expected: int | None, reported: bool, installed: int | None) -> str:
+    """Where one package a device is told to carry stands against its report."""
+    if expected is None:
+        return "unreadable"
+    if not reported:
+        # Named now, and not in the report: the policy moved on after it.
+        return "unreported"
+    if installed is None:
+        return "absent"
+    if installed < expected:
+        return "behind"
+    return "current" if installed == expected else "ahead"

+
+def _drift_view(report: <redacted>_store.Report, expected: dict[str, int | None]) -> dict:
+    """Each package `install-apps` names for this device, against what it reported.
+
+    ONLY WHAT DEVICEFLEET SHIPS. The expectation is `install-apps` and nothing
+    else, so a package the device reports that device-fleet does not install - a
+    Play-managed application, say - is never drift. device-fleet cannot update it,
+    and a row saying it is behind would be a promise nothing here can keep.
+    """
+    installed = {p.package: p.version_code for p in report.packages}
+    packages = [
+        {

+            "expected_version_code": wanted,

+            "state": _package_state(wanted, package in installed, installed.get(package)),

+    return _drift_view(report, policy.expected_versions(install_apps))

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Tickets waiting over two hours on a limited paid rung move to the strongest available free lane in their tier, while keeping the paid rung untried.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests

## Why
A lane pull request whose fix rounds failed climbs the model ladder to a paid rung (Claude, GPT), and waits there while every lane serving that model is at its limit. On 2026-10-20 the station logged "waits: no free lane takes model claude" 1,626 times and "... model gpt" 896 times in the newest 3,000 waits, and eight open lane pull requests with a failing review (another repo's 1126, 1272, 1284, 1081, 1119 among them) sat 6 to 67 hours while the free lanes took new tickets. The paid lanes were out for the day (API credits spent, subscriptions at their limits), so the climb bought nothing.

## Summary


## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A ticket waiting for a paid rung whose lanes are all limited for over the set time is briefed to the strongest untried free lane that is up.
- [x] A paid rung that frees up within the set time is still waited for.
- [x] A test that fails without the change covers both.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- How limits are measured, and the order of the ladder.
Part of ISSUE-705.
