body:
## Why
At agent scale a person cannot read every line of every lane PR, and should not: the operator reviews intent, the review bot and tests check the lines. Today a lane PR body is the ticket text plus a footer, so the reader has to work out from the diff what actually changed in behavior and how risky it is. Changes also differ in consequence: a docs-only or tests-only change is cheap to land, while a change under a sensitive path (deploy manifests, credentials handling, the merge and close code of Loom itself) deserves more scrutiny. Loom has no notion of either. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- `bus/change_class.py`: classify a PR's changed files into one class, highest wins: `sensitive` (any path matching the repo's sensitive globs), `logic`, `tests` (only test files: the existing test-file rule from ISSUE-185), `docs` (only `*.md`, `docs/`, `LICENSE`, `*.txt`). Sensitive globs come from `.loom/sensitive-paths` in the repo (one glob per line, `#` comments), read from the default branch; none means no sensitive class.
- The lane runner writes an `## Intent` section at the top of every lane PR body: the class, one line per behavior change taken from the lane's final summary (or the ticket's What when the lane gave none), and the counts of files by class. It replaces nothing else in the body.
- The PR gets a `class:<name>` label (created by `bus/labels.py`).
- Add `.loom/sensitive-paths` to this repo naming `bus/brain.py`, `bus/factory.py`, `bus/proof.py`, `lanes/mac/install.sh` and `.github/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: each class from a file list (docs only, tests only, mixed logic, one sensitive path wins over everything), globs read from `.loom/sensitive-paths` with comments ignored, and the Intent section rendered at the top of the body. Each fails without the change.
- [ ] Every lane PR opened after the deploy carries an Intent section and exactly one `class:` label.
- [ ] docs/LANES.md describes the classes and the sensitive-paths file.

Size: M

## Out of scope
Changing merge rules by class (a separate ticket); detecting comment-only edits inside code files.

+# One glob per line; lines starting with # are comments. A pattern ending
+# in / is a directory prefix. Read from the default branch. Any changed
+# file matching one of these makes the whole change class:sensitive.

index 00000000..6c852d56
--- /dev/null
+++ b/bus/change_class.py
@@ -0,0 +1,230 @@
+"""Classify a pull request's changed files into one change class.
+
+Highest wins: sensitive, logic, tests, docs.
+
+- sensitive: any path matching the repo's sensitive globs, read from
+  .loom/sensitive-paths on the default branch (one glob per line,
+  lines starting with # are comments). No file means no sensitive class.
+- logic: any other behavior-carrying file (not docs, not a test file).
+- tests: only test files (the test-file rule from the no-test check:
+  a test or tests folder in the path, or test_, _test., .test. or
+  .spec. in the name).
+- docs: only *.md, docs/, LICENSE, *.txt.
+
+The lane runner writes an ## Intent section at the top of every lane PR
+body with the class, one line per behavior change, and the counts of
+files by class. The PR also gets a class:<name> label.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import fnmatch
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import PurePosixPath
+from typing import Dict, List, Sequence
+
+CLASSES = ("sensitive", "logic", "tests", "docs")
+SENSITIVE_FILE = ".loom/sensitive-paths"
+SUMMARY_FILE = ".loom/summary.md"
+
+DOC_EXTS = (".md", ".txt")
+
+
+def parse_patterns(text: str) -> List[str]:
+    """Globs from a sensitive-paths file body; # comments and blanks ignored."""
+    out: List[str] = []
+    for line in (text or "").replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").split("\n"):
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        out.append(stripped)
+    return out
+
+
+def load_patterns(path: str) -> List[str]:
+    """Globs from a sensitive-paths file on disk; missing file means []."""
+    try:
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+            return parse_patterns(fh.read())
+    except OSError:
+        return []
+
+
+def is_docs(path: str) -> bool:
+    lowered = (path or "").lower().strip()
+    if not lowered:
+        return False
+    base = lowered.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+    if base == "license":
+        return True
+    if lowered == "license":
+        return True
+    if lowered.endswith(DOC_EXTS):
+        return True
+    if lowered == "docs" or lowered.startswith("docs/"):
+        return True
+    return False
+
+
+_TEST_FOLDERS = {"test", "tests", "t", "spec", "__tests__"}
+_TEST_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^test_|_test\.|\.test\.|\.spec\.")
+
+
+def is_test(path: str) -> bool:
+    """The existing test-file rule: a test/tests folder in the path or a
+    test-like file name."""
+    lowered = (path or "").lower()
+    if not lowered:
+        return False
+    folders, _, name = lowered.rpartition("/")
+    if bool(_TEST_FOLDERS & set(folders.split("/"))):
+        return True
+    if name.startswith("test"):
+        return True
+    return bool(_TEST_NAME_RE.search(name))
+
+
+def is_sensitive(path: str, patterns: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
+    """Does path match any sensitive glob? A pattern ending in / is a
+    directory prefix (matches the dir itself and everything under it)."""
+    p = (path or "").strip()
+    if not p or not patterns:
+        return False
+    norm = p[2:] if p.startswith("./") else p
+    if not norm:
+        return False
+    for pat in patterns:
+        pat = (pat or "").strip()
+        if not pat:
+            continue
+        if pat.endswith("/"):
+            prefix = pat.rstrip("/")
+            if not prefix:
+                continue
+            if norm == prefix or norm.startswith(prefix + "/"):
+                return True
+            continue
+        if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(norm, pat):
+            return True
+        try:
+            if PurePosixPath(norm).match(pat):
+                return True
+        except (ValueError, IndexError):
+            pass
+        base = norm.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(base, pat):
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def file_class(path: str, patterns: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str:
+    """The class of one file: sensitive, tests, docs, else logic."""
+    if is_sensitive(path, patterns):
+        return "sensitive"
+    if is_test(path):
+        return "tests"
+    if is_docs(path):
+        return "docs"
+    return "logic"
+
+
+def count_by_class(files: Sequence[str],
+                   patterns: Sequence[str] = ()) -> Dict[str, int]:
+    counts = {name: 0 for name in CLASSES}
+    for path in files or []:
+        counts[file_class(str(path), patterns)] += 1
+    return counts
+
+
+def classify(files: Sequence[str], patterns: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str:
+    """One class for a file list, highest wins. Empty means docs."""
+    counts = count_by_class(files, patterns)
+    if counts["sensitive"]:
+        return "sensitive"
+    if counts["logic"]:
+        return "logic"
+    if counts["tests"]:
+        return "tests"

+
+## Change classes and the Intent section
+
+Every lane pull request opens with an `## Intent` section at the top of
+its body, followed by the ticket sections. The section names the change
+class, one line per behavior change, and the counts of files by class:
+
+```
+## Intent
+Class: logic
+- Fix the thing for every user
+Files: 1 logic, 1 tests
+```
+
+The behavior lines come from the lane's final summary: the agent writes
+one line per behavior change to `.loom/summary.md` at the top of its
+tree (the runner tells it to, reads it, and never commits it). When the
+lane left no summary, the runner falls back to the ticket's `What`
+section, one line per non-empty line.
+
+One class covers the whole pull request, highest wins:
+
+- `sensitive`: any changed file matches `.loom/sensitive-paths` in the
+  repo (one glob per line, `#` comments, a trailing `/` is a directory
+  prefix), read from the default branch. A missing file means no
+  sensitive class. Sensitive changes deserve extra scrutiny.
+- `logic`: anything else behavior-carrying (code, config, scripts).
+- `tests`: only test files (a `test` or `tests` folder in the path, or
+  `test_`, `_test.`, `.test.` or `.spec.` in the name).
+- `docs`: only `*.md`, `docs/`, `LICENSE`, `*.txt`.
+
+The pull request carries exactly one `class:<name>` label, created like
+the other labels by `bus/labels.py`. Classification never changes merge
+rules; it only tells the reader how risky the change is.

body:
## Why

The operator asked why so many pull requests stay open. Of 31 open on 2026-10-20, six lane pull requests were green (checks and review pass, no open threads) and still bouncing: the factory sends a pull request back when its body leaves ticket criteria unticked (ISSUE-1111), but `_send_back` posts the generic `FIX_NOTES` ("it has failing checks, open review threads or a conflict with the default branch, listed below") and lists nothing, because there are no checks or threads to list. The unticked criteria go only to `station.log`. The lane has nothing to act on, changes nothing or ends without a commit, and the same pull request comes back on the same lane: ISSUE-1117 six rounds, media-library ISSUE-301 six, review-bot ISSUE-1312 five. `stuck()` only counts repeated threads, checks or a missing test, so these never climbed the model ladder.

## Summary

- `bus/factory.py`: `unticked_notes` lists each unticked criterion under `UNTICKED_HEADING` and says to build it with a test or tick it, or end its line with "; not built: <reason>". `_send_back` posts it for an unticked send-back.
- `stuck()` climbs when the last round's note named a criterion that is still unticked, as it does for a repeated thread or a missing test.
- A criterion the written-text check refuses (a closing keyword, a path) does not stop the send-back: the generic note goes out and the station logs why.
- `tests/test_bus_factory.py`: the note names the unticked criteria and not the ticked or Live ones; a second unticked round climbs; a refused criterion still goes back. The first two fail on main.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A green pull request with unticked criteria goes back with each one named and the two ways to clear it.
- [x] A second round that leaves a named criterion unticked climbs the ladder.
- [x] The full suite passes (2535 tests), and the new tests fail without the change.

Size: S

## Out of scope

- Sensitive-class pull requests waiting on the brain, and pull requests past the ladder waiting for a strong lane; separate causes.

Loom ticket none (a factory fault found in the 2-hour tally), lane operator-session, model claude-opus-5-5.

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Answer-deliverable briefs post validated diagnosis answers on tickets and move them to loom:answered without pushing or opening a pull request.
- The brain status report includes answered tickets for review.
- The station acknowledges completed answer briefs without looking for a pull request or posting a duplicate comment.
Files: 1 sensitive, 5 logic, 3 tests, 2 docs

## Why
On 2026-10-14 the agy lane answered a diagnosis ticket (game-orchestrator ISSUE-974) with an exact root cause: the 11.3-hour equip hold is a 3-try limit counted over a 12-hour window. The runner reported the run `[work] agent made no commit` and the answer stayed in a local log; the station moved the ticket to another lane, and the brain called the lane unable to crack it until the operator asked how that was known. A ticket whose deliverable is an answer, not a code change, has no way to come back today.

## Summary
- A brief may say `Deliverable: answer` (a header line, validated like the others). For such a ticket the agent writes its answer to `.loom/answer.md` at the top of the tree.
- The runner posts that file, checked by the same written-text checks as other posts (ASCII, no closing keywords, no local paths, no review bot handle), as one comment on the ticket, moves the ticket to `loom:pr`-equivalent review (`loom:answered`), and reports done, not failed. No branch or pull request is opened.
- Without `Deliverable: answer`, a run with no commit fails as today; with it and no answer file, it fails with "no answer written".
- `bus.brain status` lists answered tickets for the brain to accept (close or verify) or send back.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test runs a fake agent that writes `.loom/answer.md` on a `Deliverable: answer` brief and shows one comment posted with its text, the ticket labelled `loom:answered`, and no push or pull request.
- [ ] A test shows an answer with a local home path or a closing keyword is refused and the run fails with that reason.
- [ ] A test shows a brief without the header and no commit still fails as today.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Changing how code tickets open pull requests.
- Choosing which tickets are answer tickets (the brain's brief).

## Why
The operator asked why the brain will not disambiguate their Discord messages. The station files each message on the goal it names (a reference, a number, or a title word) and otherwise on the default goal; it does no reading. Nothing told the brain that a note filed on the default goal may concern another goal or Loom itself, so a message like "fix the review bot noise" would be handled as WoW work. Part of ISSUE-30.

- [ ] A note filed on the default goal about another goal is acted on under that goal, and the reply names it

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Roster cast failures now record spell id, spell name, and SpellCastResult constant in hourly coalesced orchestrator_event rows through a SendCastResult core hook.
- The cast failure hook exposes the explicit target to scripts and excludes successes and non-roster bots from recording.
Files: 4 logic, 1 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The <redacted> computes cast failure reasons (e.g., 'Must have a Axe equipped') in `SendCastResult` but writes them nowhere observable, so diagnosing repeating client errors required screenshots and manual effort instead of a one-line SQL query.

## Summary
Add a small core patch exposing a script hook at `SendCastResult` (`Spell.cpp:3546`/`:3854`) so failure reasons (spell id and result) are available to scripts. The `orchestrator_event` table (`kind = 'cast_fail'`, `subject_id` = spell, `detail` = reason, hourly `bucket` with `occurrences`) already reserves the schema; only the producer is missing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new `SendCastResult` script hook exposes the spell id, cast result, and target to scripts
- [ ] Failed casts by roster characters record character, spell, and failure reason into `orchestrator_event` with `kind = 'cast_fail'`
- [ ] The axe-error scenario is answerable by SQL with no client running
- [ ] Volume stays bounded: roster-scoped, deduplicated per hour, and the 500 random bots are never recorded
- [ ] The patch carries its own justification and an upstream PR link once one exists

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Recording successful casts. The question is always what is failing.
- Playerbot AI changes.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The Go datapath's control socket now accepts max_kbps per link, so a leg the agent caps gets a token bucket; changing the cap applies in place without re-dialling, an unchanged cap keeps its bucket across resyncs, and a negative cap rejects the whole sync.
- PathConfig gains carrier, plan_name, plan_type, billing_day and expected_kbps, read from link-bonder.toml and published per leg in /api/status; legs.json values win for display and are not listed as overrides.
- A billing_day set in link-bonder.toml now moves the leg's usage period boundary when legs.json does not set one.
- legs.json (the phone app's leg edits) now accepts expected_kbps as a descriptive field.
- The dashboard's link line shows the carrier and plan name when they are set.
- A phone on the LAN that reports link "ethernet" can POST /api/legs/pair to get a six-digit code; the operator approves it with POST /api/legs/pair/approve (bearer token), and the phone's next ask with that code returns the console token once, to the same address.
- /api/status lists pending pairing requests under pairing_requests, without their codes.
Files: 9 logic, 3 tests, 2 docs

## Why
The operator wants per-leg plan identity and control so the dashboard is accurate and a cheap plan is never touched unless everything else is down. Specific gaps: no throughput cap per leg, no plan metadata fields beyond label, and no handshake for ethernet-discovered phones.

## Summary
Implement a token bucket rate limiter per link in the Go datapath scheduler using `max_kbps` from `PathConfig`. Add plan metadata fields (carrier, plan name, plan type, billing day, cap, expected throughput) to `PathConfig` and expose them in the console. Implement ethernet-detected phone pairing handshake depending on legacy no. 31 and no. 33.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Token bucket rate limiter enforced in scheduler using `max_kbps` from `PathConfig` per link
- [ ] Plan metadata fields added to `PathConfig` struct and surfaced in console/agent output
- [ ] Ethernet-detected phone triggers pairing handshake flow

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Per-leg history beyond current in-memory series
- GPS-tagged leg metrics
- Operator UI for tier/priority/cap in companion app
Rewritten from issue 134.

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- check.fleet-invariants no longer reads the datadog namespace (datadog-cluster-agent replica and coverage invariants removed), so the check stops dying on the retired agent and failing closed on every run.
- The workload-version and node-version coverage invariants are removed too: they read Datadog series fed only by the retired agent and the emitters disabled on 2026-10-05, so they could only fail.
- The workflow no longer re-runs on edits to the frozen datadog-agent values.yaml.
- A new unit test parses check_invariants.py and fails if any invariant reads a Datadog namespace or workload, the datadog-agent values, or a retired agent-fed series.
Files: 4 logic, 2 tests

## Why
The scheduled `check.fleet-invariants` workflow has failed on every run on main since 2026-10-13: its step runs `kubectl get deploy datadog-cluster-agent -n datadog`, which fails because Datadog was shut down on 2026-10-05 and its agents removed, and the check then reports "the check produced no violation count - treating as a violation (fail-closed)". A permanently red scheduled check makes main look broken: on 2026-10-14 the Loom factory's post-merge revert blamed the newest deploy merge for it and opened a revert PR that would have undone a working deploy (closed by hand). Refs ISSUE-5294.

## Summary
- Remove the Datadog cluster agent invariant (and any other Datadog-agent invariant) from the fleet-invariants check, since Datadog is retired.
- Keep fail-closed for the remaining invariants: a check that cannot compute its count still fails.
- A test for the invariant list that fails while a Datadog invariant is present.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test asserts no fleet invariant reads the datadog namespace or a Datadog deployment; it fails on the current main.
- [ ] The remaining invariants still fail closed when their count cannot be read (existing tests pass).
- [ ] Live: the next scheduled check.fleet-invariants run on main passes.

Size: S

## Out of scope
Reinstalling Datadog (never); other invariants.

+"""No fleet invariant may depend on the retired Datadog agent (ISSUE-5347).
+
+The Datadog Helm release was uninstalled on 2026-10-05 (see
+production/<redacted>/manifests/datadog-agent/NOT_INSTALLED), and the emitters whose
+Datadog series the version-coverage invariants read were disabled the same
+day. check_invariants.py still ran `kubectl get deploy datadog-cluster-agent
+-n datadog`; kubectl() exits on a failed read, so the script died before
+writing any count, the workflow fail-closed to violations=1, and main showed
+red on every run from then on.
+
+check_invariants.py does its kubectl and Datadog IO at import time, so it is
+read here as source (ast) rather than imported. Only the literal ARGUMENTS of
+calls are inspected: the module docstring and comments may still describe the
+old incident without tripping this.
+
+Uses stdlib `unittest.TestCase` (ISSUE-2544: `unittest discover` drops bare
+test functions).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ast
+import os
+import unittest
+
+SCRIPT = os.path.join(
+    os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "check_invariants.py"
+)
+
+# Series that only the retired agent (container.uptime, read by the software
+# inventory emitter) or the emitters disabled with it ever produced. An
+# invariant that asserts their presence can only fail now.
+RETIRED_SERIES = (
+    "container.uptime",
+    "custom.software.instance",
+    "custom.k8s_node.report",
+)
+
+
+def _call_name(node: ast.Call) -> str:
+    func = node.func
+    if isinstance(func, ast.Name):
+        return func.id
+    if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
+        return func.attr
+    return ""
+
+
+def _string_args(node: ast.Call) -> list[str]:
+    """Every string literal anywhere inside the call's arguments."""
+    found = []
+    for arg in [*node.args, *(kw.value for kw in node.keywords)]:
+        for sub in ast.walk(arg):
+            if isinstance(sub, ast.Constant) and isinstance(sub.value, str):
+                found.append(sub.value)
+    return found
+
+
+def _calls(name: str) -> list[list[str]]:
+    with open(SCRIPT) as fh:
+        tree = ast.parse(fh.read(), filename=SCRIPT)
+    return [
+        _string_args(node)
+        for node in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and _call_name(node) == name
+    ]
+
+
+class NoDatadogAgentInvariantTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_the_scan_sees_the_script_kubectl_reads(self) -> None:
+        # Guards the guard: if the AST walk found no kubectl calls at all, the
+        # assertions below would pass vacuously.
+        reads = _calls("kubectl")
+        self.assertTrue(any("nodes" in args for args in reads), reads)
+
+    def test_no_kubectl_read_touches_the_datadog_namespace_or_a_datadog_workload(
+        self,
+    ) -> None:
+        for args in _calls("kubectl"):
+            for value in args:
+                self.assertNotIn(
+                    "datadog",
+                    value.lower(),
+                    f"kubectl{tuple(args)} reads a Datadog resource; the agent "
+                    "was uninstalled 2026-10-05 and this read fails every run",
+                )
+
+    def test_no_invariant_reads_the_datadog_agent_values(self) -> None:
+        for args in _calls("load_yaml"):
+            for value in args:
+                self.assertNotIn("datadog-agent", value, args)
+
+    def test_no_invariant_queries_a_series_only_the_retired_agent_fed(
+        self,
+    ) -> None:
+        for args in _calls("get_json"):
+            for value in args:
+                for series in RETIRED_SERIES:
+                    self.assertNotIn(
+                        series,
+                        value,
+                        f"{series} stopped arriving when Datadog was retired; "
+                        "a coverage check on it can only fail",
+                    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
